src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_cd116_500k
cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 116th Congress's districts (its file says session 116). The Bureau published no file of the 117th Congress's districts, the Congress the 2020 election chose.
rec: Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission 2012 congressional map (nine districts, the new ninth after the 2010 census)

Loyola Law School, Redistricting and Voting Rights: Arizona (secondary: 2012 maps approved 2012-01-17 by 3-2, precleared 2012-04-09 (Congress) and 2012-04-26 (legislative); 2021 maps adopted 2021-12-22, finalized 2022-01-18 (Congress) and 2022-01-21 (legislative))

Approved 2012-01-17 by a 3-2 vote; precleared 2012-04-09 (secondary summary: the Commission's own site returns 403 to scripts). Used 2012 through 2020. Kind is secondary because I could not open an official page for the congressional map. Census file: the Bureau's user note says its products hold the 116th Congress and the 2018 election-year legislative lines and none of the later changes; the cached cb_2020 files carry CDSESSN 116 / LSY 2018. Cached files: cb_2020 cd116 and cb_2022 cd118 share none of the 9 shapes.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2020 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2018 legislative session year. The Bureau published no file of the lines in use for 2020. Where a state's lines changed in between, the check below or the plan cited stops the map.
rec: Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission 2012 legislative map; 30 districts
U.S. Supreme Court, Harris v. Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission, 578 U.S. 253 (2016) (copy at Cornell LII): the Commission's revised legislative plan, adopted 3-2, precleared 2012-04-26

Arizona's 30 legislative districts each elect one senator and two representatives, so the Senate and House layers have the same lines. Approved 2012-01-17 (secondary date; the Supreme Court opinion confirms the 3-2 adoption and the 2012-04-26 preclearance). Used 2012 through 2020. Census file: the Bureau's user note says its products hold the 116th Congress and the 2018 election-year legislative lines and none of the later changes; the cached cb_2020 files carry CDSESSN 116 / LSY 2018.
